text:
For a high–energy γ-ray of energy E to annihilate with a CMB photon of energy ε into an e⁺e⁻ pair, the Mandelstam variable s must reach the pair–production threshold  

s ≥ (2 mₑc²)² .

For two photons colliding head-on (the most effective configuration)  

s = 2Eε(1 − cosθ)  with θ = π  ⇒  (1 − cosθ) = 2  
⇒ s = 4Eε .

Setting this equal to the threshold value,

4Eε = (2mₑc²)² = 4(mₑc²)²  
⇒ E = (mₑc²)² / ε .

Insert the numbers  

mₑc² = 0.511 MeV = 5.11 × 10⁵ eV  
ε (average CMB photon energy) = 10⁻³ eV

E = (5.11 × 10⁵ eV)² / (10⁻³ eV)  
  = (2.61 × 10¹¹ eV²) / (10⁻³ eV)  
  = 2.61 × 10¹⁴ eV  
  = 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV .

Thus γ-rays with energies of about 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV (2.6 × 10¹⁴ eV) will have their lifetimes limited by annihilation on the CMB.

Answer: B
